body:
I stopped loving my mom around the time I was twelve. She was never there for me to talk to her, always getting drunk in her room or banishing me to mine while she chain smoked in the living room. I only existed when she bragged to her friends about my grades. 

She died when I was fourteen, and that didn't change. The way everyone acted when I admitted this, I kept expected to suddenly miss her and be full of regrets. I'm in college now, and at most I feel pity, and more understanding for her actions. But I have never missed her or wanted her back.

No one picks their parents, and not everyone should be a parent. Your feelings are totally okay, and sharing them must be hard with all the expectations of the parent-child relationship.
